title: Story Web
description: A timeline network of thirty South Asian works and writers, from the Valmiki Ramayana and the Sangam poems to Heart Lamp (2025), colored by language group. Links show retellings, translations and responses, such as the Ramayana's Tamil, Bangla, Awadhi, Nepali and Javanese tellings and the Panchatantra's journey into Arabic as Kalila wa Dimna. Learners click works to read cards and filter by language.
creator: Aaryav Sharma
subject: South Asian cultures
Literature
Oral tradition
Epics and fables
Translation
publisher: Roots & Rivers: An Interactive Guide to South Asian Cultures for High School Students
audience: Students, Educators, South Asian student club leaders
learningObjectives: Trace how the Ramayana was retold in Tamil, Bangla, Awadhi, Nepali and Javanese.
Trace how the Panchatantra traveled into Middle Persian and Arabic as Kalila wa Dimna.
Compare which languages and eras South Asian works come from, including writing in English and in translation.
prerequisites: Knowing that an epic is a long story poem
Basic idea of translation from one language to another
keyQuestions: Which Ramayana is the real one, if there are many tellings?
How did a Sanskrit book of animal fables reach the Arab world and Europe?
How can one poet belong to more than one country?
misconceptions: South Asian literature is all religious.
Urdu poetry is only about love.
English writing is not real South Asian literature.
